A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plan-and-Budget research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on MATH-500, NaturalInstructions and TravelPlanner in Tables 3–5, plus difficulty-stratified analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations with an 8B planner, Certaindex comparisons, latency measurements and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The decomposition, difficulty weighting, decay schedulers and guided reasoning procedure remain unchanged. Renaming BBAM to BAM and clarifying that inference does not use Monte Carlo sampling do not establish a procedural change. The different planner size is an experimental configuration change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical reasoning, instruction-following and tool-free itinerary-planning coverage using MATH-500, NaturalInstructions and TravelPlanner. The added analyses vary configurations and measurements within these retained tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds Certaindex as an evaluated early-termination comparator on MATH-500 for DS-Qwen-32B, QwQ-32B and DS-LLaMA-70B (Table 7). The existing Vanilla, Global Budget and planned comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: The main evaluations switch from LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct planning to LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, retaining the 70B configuration in the appendix. v3 adds A/T evaluation, latency measurement and a budget-grid experiment. Its reported completion-token definition explicitly includes planning tokens; this does not establish that retained results were recomputed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained scheduler comparisons and TravelPlanner difficulty analysis, v3 adds planner sensitivity, E3-versus-A/T robustness, prompted-budget sensitivity and planning-versus-generation latency decomposition (Section 5.3 and Appendix F.2–F.5). Table 11 tests realized token usage, rather than accuracy robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs and report means and standard deviations for benchmark scores and token usage. Additional result rows retain this practice; no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure appears.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 3–5 are numerically retained as v3 Tables 12–14. v3 adds extensive results with the 8B planner, plus Certaindex, latency, A/T and budget-sensitivity results. For example, QwQ-32B's MATH-500 cosine E3 is 3.40 with the 8B planner, while the earlier 70B-planner value of 3.93 remains in Table 12; these are different configurations.

T1.justification: The uncertainty decomposition, power-law assumption, E3 definition, allocation equations and derivations are retained. v3 expands the Bayesian motivation and explanation of homogeneous versus heterogeneous exponents, including numerical determination of lambda, but does not replace the existing derivation or correct its heterogeneous allocation formula.

C1.justification: The headline maximum E3 improvement changes from 187.5% to 193.8%, and the introduction narrows the stated reasoning-model range from 32B–200B to 32B–70B. Its asserted entropy correlations are removed. The central contribution of training-free planning and adaptive local budgeting remains.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the introduction's entropy-correlation account with explanations involving redundant equivalent reasoning paths and fragile intermediate conclusions. Appendix C explicitly presents Bayesian uncertainty as a theoretical lens without inference-time posterior sampling. New analyses support additional interpretations about planner independence, metric robustness and practical runtime savings; the extra planner-call limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the query-budget formula and tested grid in Table 11, explicitly discloses the absence of inference-time Monte Carlo sampling, and documents access and licensing for the 8B planner. It adds a reproducibility statement. The code-link destination, hardware description and substantive prompt templates are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against Certaindex, references earlier A/T evaluation including s1, and cites Kaplan and Hoffmann to motivate power-law behavior. The main related-work organization and contribution positioning remain. Publication updates and the changed author ordering for LoRA-Ensemble do not represent new cited work.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and much of the prose remain. v3 renames BBAM to BAM, rewrites selected introduction and theory-to-practice passages, reorganizes the appendices, and adds reproducibility, ethics, acknowledgements and LLM-usage statements.

P2.justification: v3 adds latency, Certaindex, metric-comparison and budget-grid tables, while relocating the earlier main results to Tables 12–14. Figures 1, 3 and 4 are redrawn or relabeled, and the conference format changes headers, typography, table presentation and prompt-box pagination.

improvement.justification: The weaker-planner evaluation and measured latency breakdown strengthen evidence that benefits survive reduced planner capability and planning overhead, addressing gaps in v2. However, new reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: QwQ-32B's NaturalInstructions uniform E3 is 1.98 in Table 4 but 1.75 in Table 9, and Table 6 supports roughly 34–42% end-to-end latency savings rather than the claimed 38–44%. The added evidence improves the paper, but does not establish a major overall improvement.
